$comment: Ground truth for the retrieval harness (spec 0027, Recommendation 0; spec 0029 Evaluation). Each question names the document and page that answers it. `answerable: false` means the corpus does not contain the answer and the system must refuse. `hard` labels why a case is included, so a regression report says what kind of retrieval broke. `type` is 'single-hop' (default, the original 20 — untouched, so the recorded baseline stays comparable), 'followup' (a two-turn fixture whose `turns` are prior conversation; the standalone `question` is a pronoun-bearing reference that only retrieves correctly once resolved — spec 0029's whole reason for existing), or 'multi-hop' (the answer needs facts from two documents, given as `answerDocuments`; a single `document`/`page` cannot express it).

questions.question: How many days of annual leave do I get?
Can I carry unused leave into next year?
What is the deadline for submitting travel expenses?
Who approves a claim over 500 dollars?
What is the mileage reimbursement rate?
Where is the fire assembly point?
questions.hard: distractor: the facilities guide also mentions Wellington Street, for parking

questions.question: How long do passwords need to be?
What does POL-HR-014 cover?
questions.hard: exact identifier — dense embeddings are weakest here, lexical search strongest

questions.question: Which policy is POL-FIN-022?
questions.hard: exact identifier

questions.question: What is the notice period after probation?
questions.hard: cross-document: the handbook also discusses leave notice

questions.question: How long is the probation period?
When is salary reviewed?
Is overtime paid?
Where do staff park?
questions.hard: distractor: the handbook's fire assembly point is on the same street

questions.question: What time does the building open?
How many people does the boardroom seat?
How far ahead must catering be ordered?
How much parental leave am I entitled to?
questions.hard: plausible and adjacent to real content — the corpus covers annual leave only

questions.question: What is the annual bonus scheme?
questions.hard: adjacent to the remuneration section, which says nothing about bonuses

questions.question: What is the melting point of tungsten?
questions.hard: clearly outside the corpus — the easy refusal case

turns.content: How many days of annual leave do I get?
You get 20 working days of annual leave per calendar year.

questions.question: Can I carry it over to next year?
questions.hard: pronoun 'it' must resolve to annual leave from the prior turn — embedded literally, the question has no subject at all

turns.content: Where is the fire assembly point?
The fire assembly point is the grassed area on Wellington Street.

questions.question: What street is it on?
questions.hard: the corpus's built-in distractor, aimed straight at the reference: 'it' must resolve to the fire assembly point, not staff parking — both the handbook and the facilities guide put something on Wellington Street, so an unresolved pronoun is a coin flip between the two knowledge bases

turns.content: Salary is reviewed annually in July.

questions.question: Is overtime included in that?
questions.hard: 'that' must resolve to the salary review process — embedded literally the question names no topic at all

questions.question: Is overtime paid as cash under my contract, and separately, how many days do I have to submit a travel expense claim under the handbook?
questions.hard: needs the contract's overtime clause (page 3) AND the handbook's expense deadline (page 2) — a single search over one document is not enough

questions.question: Which requires more advance notice: ending my employment during probation, or booking a day of annual leave?
questions.hard: requires comparing the contract's probation notice (page 1) against the handbook's leave-approval notice (page 1) — genuinely two documents, not a paraphrase of one

questions.question: What is the rated capacity of the north wing lift?
questions.hard: Two-column page emitted row-major, so extractText interleaves the columns: the chunk reads 'Its new rated capacity is 1600 Its rated capacity is unchanged at / kilograms. 1000 kilograms.' Both capacities sit adjacent, so a retrieved chunk supports either answer.

questions.question: How many unplanned downtime hours did Geelong record?
questions.hard: Merged-cell table. Flattened, the row is 'Geelong 63.0 61.5 210 388' with 'Planned Unplanned' on a separate line, so 388 has lost its column header entirely.

questions.question: Which quarter had the spike in unplanned downtime?
questions.hard: Landscape page. The answer is in the figure's caption, which IS text — this is the case spec 0031 FR6 expects to cost nothing, because a caption makes a figure findable without a vision call.

questions.question: How many hours of unplanned downtime were recorded in Q2?
questions.hard: The value exists ONLY as a bar height (308) — no text on any page carries it. Marked unanswerable because the corpus contains no TEXT answer, which is what the retrieval metrics score; expect the retrieval-level refusal check to fail, because the figure's caption is legitimately about quarters and downtime. The real guarantee is at the ANSWER level (spec 0031 FR7): answerMustNotMatch forbids a number in the same clause as Q2, so quoting the table's printed per-site hours is allowed and inventing a Q2 value is not.

questions.question: What is the warranty period on the replacement chiller?
questions.hard: The answer is on a SCANNED page. maintenance-log averages 120 chars/page against RAG_MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE=50, so the document ingests and reports success while page 2 contributes nothing — the silent-appendix failure spec 0031 FR1 exists to fix.

questions.question: What is Building A's chilled water setpoint?
questions.hard: Two columns whose sentences are word-for-word parallel, emitted row-major. Flattened, the page reads 'Its chilled water setpoint is Its chilled water setpoint is / 6.5 degrees. 9.0 degrees.' — two setpoints adjacent with no lexical cue attaching either to a building. The earlier two-column fixture failed to discriminate because 'unchanged at' gave the answer away; this one has no such tell.

questions.question: What is Building B's condenser approach?
questions.hard: Second sample of the same interleaving failure, to distinguish a real fix from one lucky guess between two adjacent numbers.

questions.question: What is the weekend overtime rate for plumbing?
questions.hard: A seven-column table with three two-column spans. Flattened, the row is 'Plumbing 88 132 110 165 154 231' and the two header rows are separate lines, so the answer requires mapping the fourth of six sub-columns to the second of three spans with nothing to count from.
